snippet.title: Harry Potter: Voldemort Scenes Without CGI Effects
snippet.description:
We’ve got a special look into the brilliantly terrifying way VFX artists took on the look of Voldemort in the Harry Potter franchise. Ralph Fiennes played the role brilliantly - with a little help from that classic CGI look. From that infamous non-existent nose - to those magical spell castings - we’ve got you covered on how the Voldemort CGI was done.
This isn’t your average Harry Potter behind the scenes video - we’re taking you on the evolution of how every aspect of He Who Must Not Be Name’s visual effects work. This work took a while to master as well - with a constant eye for detail when it came to his look - and of course his surroundings. Every spell he cast got better and better in all the Harry Potter scenes as they came to the big screen. But as Tom’s appearance got less practical - his creatures became more animated. That Basilisk Harry slays in the Chamber of Secrets - was surprisingly more real than you’d think. And Nagini? Well for safety reasons - it was probably for the best that they went with full CGI on that one.
There were a lot of us at the edge of our seats - seeing the fully formed Dark Lord on the big screen. And we could never guess how his final look was actually achieved - until now. Some of these interesting facts will make you raise an eyebrow - which was not really possible for poor Ralph Fiennes!

snippet.title: The Voices Behind The Bad Guys
snippet.description:
The Bad Guys is jam-packed with a solid cast of actors. Most haven’t done a whole lot of voice acting, except for Alex Borstein. The cast was able to record together, luckily. After the few years voice actors have had, we’re sure they’re glad to be in a studio playing off of each other. Sam Rockwell’s been in another animated movie with guinea pigs, except last time he was one. Problematically, he forgot that he worked on another movie with one of his co-stars. Richard Ayoade was a perfect casting choice for Professor Marmelade. He usually plays food or animals. Awkwafina was happy to play a character who knows what she’s doing. Craig Robinson tried to improvise and they didn’t let the poor guy, but he found his own way to improvise anyway. Marc Maron admits to mostly just playing himself. Hey, if it works, it works! Why change it? Anthony Ramos got an awesome addition to his character pretty last-minute in the process. Zazie Beetz absolutely adored being able to use her eyebrows. Now you might be thinking “what do eyebrows have to do with voice acting?” A lot! Lilly Singh is another actor with an expressive face. She was happy to not have to hide that and even happier that her character reflected her so well. And Alex Borstein, who’s played Lois on Family Guy forever, really enjoyed the depth of her character. Sounds like all of the female voice actors were either loving the self-expression or the depth of plots. Let’s have more of this, please! It’s a fun video so check it out if you want to hear about tiny unicorns and cat donuts and Richard Ayoade playing an onion.

snippet.title: Twilight Cast Pranks And Behind The Scenes Bloopers
snippet.description:
There was drama, romance, and a whole lotta laughs throughout the filming of the Twilight Saga. Considering there were five movies and much of the cast was around for the majority of the time, actors got loopy and tried to liven things up a bit, playing jokes on each other and the crew members. How far did they go just to get a laugh?
While there were loads of small-scale pranks on set on the daily, one prank really was the one to end all pranks. The majority of the cast got in on this one, planning a special flash mob surprise for director Bill Condon in the middle of filming one day. With so much money on the line and a tight schedule though, it wasn’t necessarily the ideal time. How did Condon feel about it in the end? 
Robert Pattinson was pretty serious on set but he took part in some jokes - but even more so, pranks were played on HIM. Unfortunately, they often went over his head though, leaving many a joke to fall flat. While he was supportive of his castmates playing jokes and enjoyed the fun that came from them on set, when Bryce Dallas Howard enlisted him to help her pull off a big trick on the crew, Pattinson REALLY let her down. 
Kristen Stewart had to deal with the special effects quite literally raining on her parade - leaving her to feel like she was drowning on totally dry land! The set got the best of her and co-star Taylor Lautner when it came time for them to carry out a deceivingly simple task - opening a car door. And then there was GFYS - a prank that swept through the cast and crew, and likely resulted in a lot of contributions to the swear jar set up to discourage swearing around the young Mackenzie Foy. 
Making movies is hard work, but as exhibited by the Twilight team - it can also be way more fun than you’d imagine!

snippet.title: 15 Difficult Scenes To Film In Stranger Things
snippet.description:
Stranger Things has some of the most intense scenes put to screen! And that is in large part thanks to the incredible actors that bring the show to life. Millie Bobby Brown, Finn Wolfhard, Dacre Montgomery and Sadie Sink are just a few of the amazing actors that give their all into creating their characters. This level of intensity means sometimes things get dangerous on set, both physically and mentally. There are numerous examples of our favorite actors losing their voices due to screaming too much. One actor stated they lost their voice nearly every day while shooting! There were also plenty of injuries to go around. From scrapes and bruises, contacts that burned eyes, temperatures that ranged from freezing cold to scorching hot, and nauseating stunts that made actors throw up, filming these scenes was no joke. 

There was also the mental side of filming. Many of these actors were part of emotionally exhausting and mentally draining scenes. This would lead to actors crying before, during, and after shooting. Some scenes got really intense, to the point where the actors had to comfort each other when the cameras weren’t rolling. Balancing raw emotions with intense physicality was tricky at times. In one particular incident, it led to an actor putting his head through a glass window. 

We are really impressed with the commitment each of these actors have towards their roles. They gave it their all every day, and the results speak for themselves. Which scene do you think was the most intense? Let us know in the comments, and thanks for stopping by at The Things!

snippet.title: Encanto's Alternate Ending Was Originally Much Darker
snippet.description:
If you thought you cried a lot during Encanto - just know some alternate scenes nearly gave us a MUCH darker and more emotional film! We’re taking a look at all the possibilities the Encanto team considered while bringing this movie to the big screen - get ready to grab the tissues.
Losing Pedro is a heartbreaking moment in the movie and reveals a lot about Abuela Alma’s past - but in one version, there was a chance Pedro would actually pass away AT THE SAME TIME as Abuela was giving birth to the triplets. Heartbreak much? An alternate scene also saw Abuela and Mirabel having a different reconciliation conversation, one that had Abuela explaining why she was scared of the miracle for so long. Even though we see Mirabel and Abuela going head to head, an alternate storyline saw Mirabel and her mother Julieta having an epic fight, resulting in the collapse of Casita!
Seeing the Madrigal household in shambles was a tough sight to see - but alternate storyboards saw an even darker and creepier image taking the place of the beloved family home. Casita’s fate was up in the air for a while too. Some versions saw Casita burning down to the ground and seeing the house struggle with its memory, experiencing a kind of “brain fog” and losing details within the house. 
As for the characters - there were several characters that almost joined the cast who would have had a big effect on certain plot points, including Isabella’s suitor and a very different, far more intense papa Agustín. 
Encanto had a whole lot of possibilities during the making, but ultimately the team put together a very special film - but all these alternate storylines certainly have us thinking about all the possibilities there could have been!

snippet.description:
When so many fantastical creatures appear on screen, you know CGI played a huge part! Every creature we see in the world of Fantastic Beasts was brought to life with highly-detailed computer animation, but their stand-ins on set were surprisingly effective. The creatures didn’t include all the same details - but they did the trick - even if it was just a puppet head and a person holding it! Creating Gnarlark’s likeness was majorly helped by the actor he was inspired by, doing extensive motion capture sessions, including a facial motion capture session involving a whopping ninety-eight individual cameras. 
One of Eddie Redmayne’s most challenging scenes was riding the Kelpie - and even though there wasn’t an actual Kelpie insight, Redmayne was getting soaked, filming himself and his Kelpie stand-in going wild underwater! When it came to bringing Nagini to life, extra special help was called in to help. It took a whole lot of computer animators and TWO contortionists to bring this mesmerizing transition to life. 
Jacob’s apartment was full of many moving pieces - ones that could fully take care of themselves - but how did they animate it to look like such a magical build? How about the apple strudel? The production team investigated and replicated EXACTLY how a strudel would be made, floating through the air, bringing in the help of special animation tech. 
As for traveling to old-timey New York? Well CG made it a whole lot easier, but that didn’t mean there weren’t pretty special and detailed practical sets for the actors to work on. Every detail brought to life by CG makes Fantastic Beasts a more convincing and exciting world to get lost in.

snippet.title: Behind The Set Of Moon Knight
snippet.description:
Moon Knight is impressive. And no wonder! Aside from an amazing cast, there was also an amazing director on board who got an incredible crew of Egyptian artists on board to see this thing through as authentically as possible. They had access to a well of knowledge when it came to things like hieroglyphics where they filmed. It’s hard to tell the mock-sets from the real ones, isn’t it? Moon Knight makes it a bit harder to guess than something like Spider-Man: No Way Home. But trust us, there are some sets that were built. Would you have been able to guess that wasn’t actually the British Museum in London? Or that literally none of that was shot in London? It had some geography errors going on for sure but we were shocked to find out it was all filmed in Budapest! And there was one crazy detail that would have complicated filming by like… a lot. They shot at some really cool locations though like Eltz Castle and Szentendre. There’s some really cool inspiration that went into the creation of Steven Grant’s apartment that would only come from the minds of geniuses in their field. That windy road in the show is host to an incredibly dangerous event. The restaurant was not in England but it sure was dolled up to look like Soho, which apparently isn’t as hard to do as you’d expect. It just takes good location scouts. Wadi Rum has been host to a number of Disney films and also to Oscar Isaacs on more than one occasion. The sets for the show are so freaking impressive but we owe it all to the director, Mohamed Diab for that two hundred page pitch bible he put together with his wife Sarah Goher before even landing the job!

Jamie Foxx went from adoring the Spider-Man costume in The Amazing Spider-Man to adoring his own in No Way Home. Willem Dafoe, even in his sixties, could keep up with Tom Holland and the stunt work. snippet.title: Painful Costumes In Bridgerton Season 2
snippet.description:
Bridgerton is back - and so are the painful costumes! The Regency-era drama is a feast for the eyes and looks beautiful - but that beauty causes a whole lot of pain to the actors sporting the period-style and typically uncomfortable costumes. Simone Ashley had a rude awakening on her very first day on set as the leading lady, learning that some normal activities - like eating - weren’t as easy as one might expect. The corset struggle is real - and all the actors who wear them throughout the season can attest to how difficult they could make even the simplest of things, like putting on shoes. Phoebe Dynevor’s body went through the wringer once again, before her body could even fully heal from all the wear and tear from season one. 
Nicola Coughlan could be dangerous to be around when she was in heels - the actor drew blood from one of her co-stars and regularly fell over pretty randomly. The actress was also losing her hair, sort of. Let’s just say it wasn’t too surprising to stumble upon one of Penelope Featherington’s curls somewhere on set. 
Regency-era clothing made for a modern-day problem- where to put cell phones? Jonathan Bailey lets us in on a secret about where their tech hides away when the cameras are rolling. 
Those wearing corsets on set struggled to breathe at times, and the rest of the cast members got a bit of a taste of the experience as they all wore new accessories on the set - and this new look wasn’t just being sported by the actors - the whole crew came on board! 
We love watching Bridgerton in huge part because of the brilliant costumes and the fact that the actors endure all these struggles wearing them makes us appreciate the performances even more.

Ten years of filming Harry Potter provided a lot of emotional moments on set. There were many times when our favorite actors like Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson, and Rupert Grint shed a few tears. snippet.title: The Adam Project Scenes Without CGI
snippet.description:
Traveling back in time, finding your father and younger self all while trying to find and save your missing wife - you can bet CGI was a major part of The Adam Project! With a whopping budget of 116 million dollars, the production team pulled out all the stops, including massive practical effects, highly detailed sets, and custom-made tools. With all this at work, CGI came in to amplify, detail, and vamp up all the action we see!
De-aging is a tricky process and was necessary for this time-traveling film - but which actor came out looking almost unrecognizable? Sorian technology looks pretty cool - even if the weapons aren’t always what they appear to be. All those tools were designed and then 3D printed and constructed by a small company in Australia - only to get the CG treatment in the editing phase. 
Let’s talk about the big chase-fight scene, this is one that we would expect to be pretty much full CG, but the fact is, it’s actually about a fifty-fifty split! There were real hovercrafts on set, whipping through the tall woods of British Columbia and bringing to life literal high-flying action. CG was key in putting all the pieces together, from touching up the details of the hovercraft action, filling in the background and action around the car that was filmed still and in front of a blue screen, and of course, the creation of the giant spacecraft, capable of making itself invisible. 
The Adam Project is a feast for the eyes, using the best of the best to put together a visually exciting and innovative film.

snippet.title: Spider-Man No Way Home CGI Vs. The Real Scene
snippet.description:
We knew the Spider-Man: No Way Home team used a lot of CG to bring all the action to the screen, but we didn’t realize only EIGHTY frames would be without any kind of CG. From the biggest of explosions, most complicated of stunts to the subtlest details, we’re uncovering just how significant VFX use was in this movie. 
All the villains that returned from other universes received some big upgrades, many thanks to the help of CGI. Alfred Molina ditched the puppet tentacles for lightweight CG arms, which Willem Dafoe got to ride multiple different glider rigs that relied on CGI removing all the mechanics. Jamie Foxx went from full CG body to partial CG body - just how much of what we saw on screen was real? 
The days that get everyone buzzing on set involve huge explosions and practical effects. A few of the days on the Spider-Man set saw wild action, from a car being launched a hundred and fifty yards through the air to concrete pipes being smashed around.
The bridge fight between Doc Ock and Spider-Man saw CGI used in major ways and for subtle details, and the team used whatever methods they needed to make sure they did justice to the scene. Shooting footage that would see Holland sporting the CGI Iron-Spider suit included capturing the look of a metal bust made specifically so the team could see how it reacted with the light in each scene, to have the best reference point when the CG magic took over. 
No matter how big or small, every CG detail was thought through and helped to complete the incredible images we see throughout the film.
